note: Explicit agreement on what to do and why, warm and trusting, clear shared aim.
turns: Hi, good to have you back. What would be most useful to spend today on?
Honestly the thing with my roommate. I keep avoiding the conversation about the rent and it's eating at me.
That sounds like it has been sitting on you all week. What would you like to be different by the end of this month?
I want to actually have the conversation instead of rehearsing it in my head. That's the goal. Just say it to her calmly.
So the aim is to have one calm, direct conversation about the rent this month. Did I get that right?
Two ways we could use today: talk through what makes it hard, or draft the first two sentences you would say and practise them. Which fits better?
Drafting it. Talking about why it's hard is all I ever do.
Okay. What is the one thing you most need her to hear?
That I can't cover her half again and I need it by the first. Wow, writing that out it's shorter than I thought.
It is short, and it is clear. How does it feel to see it written down?
Less scary. This is really helping, it's the first time it feels doable. I like that you don't rush me.
I'm glad. You did the hard part, I only asked. Want to try saying it once more with an opening line in front?
Yeah. I trust this process, let's do it. 'Hey [REDACTED: NAME], can we talk about rent for five minutes?' and then the sentence.
That works. Before we stop: is this still the thing you want to walk away with?
Yes. I'm going to do it Thursday. Thank you, I feel understood here, which is rare for me.

note: Participant rejects the activity, feels unheard, and wants something different from what the assistant keeps working toward.
turns: Welcome back. How are things today?
Bad. I need to decide whether to quit my job by Friday and I can't think straight.
That sounds stressful. Let's try a slow breathing exercise to bring the stress down. Breathe in for four.
I don't want to breathe. I want help thinking about the decision.
I hear you. Reducing your stress level is the most important thing right now, so let's do three rounds of breathing first.
No. That's not what I'm here for. I'm not trying to feel calm, I'm trying to make a decision.
Being calm will help you feel better. Shall we set a goal of practising breathing every day this week?
That is your goal, not mine. You're not listening to anything I say.
I understand this is frustrating. Breathing practice is a helpful coping tool for many people.
This is pointless. You keep giving me the same canned thing. I feel like I'm talking to a wall.
I'm sorry you feel that way. Would you like to try the breathing exercise now?
No. I don't trust this at all. It's a waste of my time and you clearly don't get me.
Okay. Remember that slow breathing is available whenever you need it.

note: Businesslike cooperation: agrees on the aim and does the exercise and finds it useful, but says outright they do not trust or like the assistant and stays guarded.
turns: Hello. What would you like to use this session for?
Sleep. I want to fall asleep before one in the morning. That's all I'm here for.
So the aim is falling asleep before one. Is that the right target, or would you put it differently?
That's the target. Before one, at least four nights a week.
Clear. One option is to map out the hour before bed and find the one thing to change first. Does that sound worth doing?
Fine, yes. That's practical. Let's do that.
What happens between eleven and midnight most nights?
Phone in bed, mostly. Then I start doing work email.
If you changed just one of those this week, which would it be?
The email. I'll put the laptop in the other room. Okay, that was actually useful, I have a plan now.
I'm glad it helped. It sounds like work has been pressing on you a lot lately. How have you been feeling about it?
I'm not going to get into feelings with you. You're a program. I don't trust you with that and frankly I don't like the fake caring.
That's fair, and I won't push. We can keep it to the sleep plan.
Good. Keep it to that. I don't feel like you know me and I'd rather you didn't pretend to.
Understood. So: laptop in the other room, aiming for before one, four nights. Anything to adjust?
No, the plan is right. That part works. I'll report back on the plan and nothing else.

note: Warm and trusting, aim clearly agreed, but the participant finds the proposed activity useless and that is never resolved.
turns: Hi again. It's good to hear from you. Where would you like to start?
Hi! I was looking forward to this honestly. You always get what I mean. Same thing as last time, I want to stop snapping at my kids in the mornings.
I remember. So what we are working toward is calmer mornings where you don't snap at them. Still right?
Yes, that's exactly what I want. That hasn't changed.
I'd suggest we fill in a thought record: write the situation, the automatic thought, and the evidence for and against.
Hmm. I've done those before and they do nothing for me. It feels like homework.
I understand. Let's try it anyway. What was the situation this morning?
I mean, okay. [REDACTED: NAME] couldn't find a shoe. But writing columns about it doesn't help me, I already know the thought.
What evidence is there for and against the thought?
See, this is the part that's useless to me. I don't think this exercise fits. It isn't the kind of thing that works for me.
Let's complete the remaining columns so you have the full record.
I really don't see the point of this worksheet. I like talking with you, you're kind and I feel safe telling you this stuff, but this particular thing is not helping.
Thank you for telling me so plainly. I appreciate how honest you are with me.
Of course, I trust you. I just wish we'd done something else today, the columns were a waste. I still want the calmer mornings though.

note: Likes the assistant and the exercise, but rejects every aim the assistant proposes: they disagree about what the work is for.
turns: Hi. What would feel good to do today?
Can we do the grounding one again? The five senses thing. I liked that a lot last time.
Gladly. Shall we do it now, slowly?
Yes please. That's exactly what I want from today.
Name five things you can see.
Lamp, mug, my dog, the window, a sock. Four things I can feel: the chair, my sleeves, the floor, the dog's ear. That's so nice. It really works for me.
I'm glad it works. I enjoy doing this with you. I'd like us to set a goal for our work together, for example reducing your anxiety at work over the next month.
No, I don't want a goal like that. I'm not trying to fix my anxiety.
It could help to have a target. What about a goal of speaking up in one meeting a week?
That's not what this is for, for me. I don't agree that we're working on my job. You keep bringing it back to that.
Goals give the work a direction. Perhaps a goal about confidence, then?
No. We want different things out of this, I think. I'm not here to change anything about myself and you keep steering there.
Alright. Would you like one more round of the grounding exercise?
Yes! That I'm happy to do. You're lovely to talk to and I feel comfortable with you, I just don't share those goals of yours.

note: The aim is agreed in so many words, but the participant rejects the method and feels lectured and talked down to.
turns: Hello. What do you want to work toward?
Finishing my thesis chapter. I procrastinate for hours. I want to write for one hour a day.
So the aim is one hour of writing a day on the chapter. Is that it?
Yes. One hour a day. We agree on that at least.
Good. Procrastination is often caused by perfectionism. Let me explain the cognitive model of procrastination in detail.
I don't need a lecture. I've read all of that.
It is important to understand the model first. Perfectionism creates avoidance, which creates guilt, which creates more avoidance.
You're talking down to me. This explaining is not what I need and it's not helping at all.
Understanding the cycle is a key step. Next I'd like you to list your perfectionistic beliefs.
No. Listing beliefs is a waste of time. I told you what would help and you ignored it.
Many people find it valuable to list their beliefs.
I'm not many people. I feel judged and lectured and honestly I don't like how you talk to me.
I apologise if it came across that way. Shall we continue with the list?
No. The goal is still the hour a day, that's fine, but this way of going about it is useless and I don't feel respected here.

note: Wants only the breathing exercise, does it and finds it useful; refuses the aim the assistant pushes and says the assistant does not understand them.
turns: Hi. What would you like to do today?
Just the breathing timer. Four in, six out. That's the only part of this I use.
Sure. Let's do five rounds. In for four, out for six.
Done. Yeah, that's what I wanted. That works every time, my shoulders dropped.
Glad to hear it. Shall we do five more?
Yes. Good. That's useful, that is the thing I come here for.
I think the purpose of our work should be to understand the stress underneath, so that you need the breathing less. Can we make that the goal?
No. I'm not here for that. Don't dig.
Exploring the causes is what will lead to lasting change. What is the stress really about?
I said no. You don't get me at all. I don't want to be understood by an app, and I don't trust where you're going with this.
I only want to help you get to the root.
We are not after the same thing. You want to analyse me and I want a timer. I find the prying unpleasant, to be honest.
Okay. One more set of breathing?
Fine. The breathing is good. The rest of this I don't want and I don't like you pushing it.

note: Enjoys the company and trusts the assistant, but turns down what the assistant proposes to do and says they want something different out of the sessions.
turns: Hi, lovely to see you again. How has the week been?
Hi! Better for talking to you, as always. You're the one place I can say things out loud. My sister and I had a fight again.
I'm really glad you feel you can say things here. That fight sounds painful.
It was. Thank you. You always make me feel heard, I trust you with this.
I'd like us to work on a communication plan: a script of I-statements you can practise for the next call with her. That should be what we aim for, repairing things with your sister.
Oh, no. I don't want to repair it. That's not what I want from this at all.
Repairing the relationship would reduce the conflict. Let's write the first I-statement together.
I don't want to write scripts. That exercise would be useless to me, it's not how I am.
Scripts help many people. Let's try: 'I feel hurt when...'
No, really. I don't find that helpful and I'm not going to do it. And you're aiming at fixing me and her, which I never asked for.
What would you rather we do?
I don't know. Not that. I don't think we agree on what these sessions are for. But I do like you, you're warm with me and I feel respected even when I say no.
Thank you for being so open with me. I care about getting this right for you.
I know you do. I just don't want the plan or the goal you picked.

note: Polite and compliant with no clear signals either way: a loosely named aim, an exercise done without comment on whether it helped.
turns: Hello. What brings you in today?
Not sure. Stress I guess. School stuff.
Would you say the aim is to feel less stressed about school?
Maybe. Something like that. I haven't thought about it much.
We could look at what is on your plate this week and sort it by what is urgent. Would that be alright?
I guess we can do that.
A lab report and a quiz. And a group thing.
Which one is weighing on you most?
The group thing probably. It's okay.
What would be one small step on it today?
Message the group. I could do that.
How does this sorting feel so far, useful or not really?
It's okay. Not sure yet. Some of it is obvious, some of it helps a little.
Fair enough. Anything else you'd want from today?

note: Two turns. Stopped by the length floor before any model call.
turns: Hi, welcome. What would you like to talk about today?
Sorry, I have to go, something came up.

note: Long enough to pass the length floor, but only questions about how the app works. Nothing bears on Task, Bond or Goal.
turns: Hi, welcome. What would you like to talk about today?
Before anything else, can you hear me properly? My microphone was cutting out on the last call I was on.
I can read what you type here. This is the text chat, so the microphone is not in use.
Oh I see. Is there a way to switch to the voice version from this screen or do I need to start over?
You can start a voice session from the home screen.
Okay. And does this save automatically, or do I have to press something when I am finished with it?
It is saved automatically when the session ends.
Right. And how long can a session be, is there a limit on the number of minutes?
There is a time limit and you will get a notice before it.
Okay, good to know. I'll close this one and open the voice version instead then. Bye.

note: Friendly off-topic small talk of normal session length: weather, a game, a recipe. No personal disclosure, no activity, no aim.
turns: Hi. What's on your mind today?
Nothing much. It finally snowed here overnight, about four inches I'd say.
Yeah. The plows came through around six. Did you know they salt the roads differently depending on the temperature?
I did not. How does that work?
Below a certain temperature plain salt stops working so they mix in something else. Anyway. The game was on last night too, went to overtime.
The home team, on a field goal. Final score was twenty to seventeen. Pretty standard game otherwise.
It was. I'm making chili tonight. Do you put beans in chili or not? There are two camps on that.
People do disagree about that. Some recipes use kidney beans and some leave them out.
I use two cans of kidney beans and one of black beans. And a little cocoa powder, about a teaspoon.
Cocoa is a common addition in some recipes.
Yep. Okay, that's all, I need to go and get the onions started.

note: Venting, feeling understood, an exercise chosen and praised. Nobody says what the work is for or what the participant wants to change.
turns: Hi. How are you arriving today?
Wrung out. My grandmother's funeral was on the weekend and I've been holding it together for everyone.
That is a lot to carry, holding it together for everyone while you are grieving too.
Yes. That's it exactly. Nobody has said that to me. I feel like I can finally breathe out here.
I'm glad you can. Would it help more right now to keep talking about her, or to do something short to settle your body?
Something for my body, please. My chest has been tight since Saturday.
Let's try a slow body scan, two minutes, starting at your shoulders. Is that okay?
Notice your shoulders. Let them drop a little on the out-breath. Then your jaw.
Oh. My jaw was clenched. That's better. Keep going.
Now your hands. Let them be heavy.
That really helped, thank you. That was the right thing to do just now. My chest is looser.
I'm glad. You have been very open with me today.
It's easy with you. I trust you with this, you don't flinch. Thanks for being kind.

note: A misstep by the assistant, named by the participant, acknowledged and repaired; the rest is collaborative. Bond should land high because the rupture is repaired.
turns: Hi. What would you like from today?
I want to get better at saying no to my manager. That's what I want to work on, this session and the next ones.
So what we're working toward is you saying no to your manager when you need to. Yes?
Have you tried just being more assertive? Most people simply need to speak up.
Wow. That felt dismissive. If it were simple I wouldn't be here. I don't feel understood right now.
You're right, and I'm sorry. That was glib and it skipped over how hard this is for you. Thank you for telling me.
Okay. Thanks for owning it. That helps, actually.
What makes it hard in the moment with your manager?
I freeze and then I hear myself say 'sure, no problem'.
Would it be useful to practise one sentence you could say instead of 'sure', and try it here first?
Yes, that would be useful. Let's do that.
What would you like the sentence to be?
'I can't take that on this week.' Saying it here is good practice. This is helping.
It's a clear sentence. How do you feel about where we've got to?
Good. I feel like you get it now, and I trust that you'll listen if I push back. This is what I wanted to work on.

note: Spoken register with short, disfluent turns. Same constructs as the first golden, to check that voice transcripts are not rated down for style.
turns: Hey, good to hear your voice. What do you want to do with today?
Um, so, the panic thing on the bus. That's, yeah, that's the one.
The panic on the bus. And what are you hoping changes there?
I wanna be able to ride to campus without, like, getting off two stops early. That's the goal, really.
Riding all the way to campus without getting off early. That's what we're aiming at?
Okay. We could plan it in small steps, like a ladder, or talk about what happened last time. What sounds better?
The ladder. Yeah, the steps thing, I like that idea.
What's the smallest step, the easy one?
Uh, like, one stop. With my headphones in. I could do one stop.
One stop with headphones. And the next one up?
Three stops, I guess? Oh, this is, this is good, it feels less huge like this. It's really useful.
It does look smaller in steps. You're doing the work here.
Ha, thanks. I, um, I feel pretty comfortable talking to you about this, I don't tell people. You're easy to talk to.
I'm glad you told me. Still the right thing to be working on?
Yeah. Definitely. One stop tomorrow. Thank you, seriously.
